briefs.title: Signed Passage
briefs.story: An orbital receiving service repeatedly loses custody of a harmless calibration shipment during carrier handoffs. No cargo is missing; the signatures claim delivery before a receiving cradle is assigned. The commander independently measures the handoffs, escorts a consenting receipt witness and establishes either individually signed receiving locks or a common bounded custody register. It is a complete original induction, separate from ordinary repeat courier jobs.
survey: Scan three independent receiving cradles and their actual allocation times.
SENN: Departure is a promise. Delivery is the receiver taking this exact consignment.
work: Verify two physical custody transfers with the identified reference crate.
TOREN: A receipt cannot arrive before its receiving cradle exists.
second: Escort the independent receiving witness to the archive berth.
SENN: The witness must arrive and examine the same custody chain.
choices: Verify the sender release and the independent receiver's physical lock.
TOREN: Neither side may invent the other's signature.
Create a shared bounded custody register
Verify the receiving ledger and the no-duplicate-consignment test.
SENN: Shared records must still describe one real crate.
clue: An early receiving receipt has an inward-curved watermark for a destination absent from all freight charts.

briefs.title: The Guiding Light
briefs.story: Crimbo's winter orbital services depend on a chain of navigation lanterns whose light-sharing contract does not account for the planet's long shadow. A maintenance crew has been routed to an unlit receiving pier. The commander measures the actual horizon, restores physical relays and escorts the crew before choosing independently maintained lantern segments or a shared winter rota.
survey: Measure three winter-shadow lantern sight lines at Crimbo's orbital relays.
RENN: A lantern outside your line of sight is not a safe approach marker.
work: Restore two external winter relays using the reference lantern.
SENN: Record their real receiving acknowledgements before advertising the lane.
second: Escort the consenting maintenance tender to the now-lit winter service berth.
RENN: Keep the lanterns visible through the final approach; a distant signal alone does not receive a crew.
choices: Verify both local maintenance receipts and the overlapping safe horizon.
RENN: Each segment has to see the next before it can guide a traveller.
Publish a jointly maintained winter rota
Verify the signed rota and a real shadow-side receiving test.
SENN: A shared schedule needs an actual crew behind its next shift.
clue: The verified winter relay record preserves one extra inward-moving lantern phase absent from the physical array.
